text:
elena: Quick heads-up — I want to propose a lightweight 'log escrow' flow for privileged access to SIEM exports during vuln triage and incident response. Goal: allow short-term, auditable access to decrypted logs without broad RBAC changes.
noah: high-level ask?
elena: TL;DR: requestor opens SEC ticket, two approvers (sec + oncall), create single-use presigned URL to archived logs (S3), decrypt via escrow-role that has KMS:Decrypt but only when invoked by the presign lambda. Access TTL 24h and download count limited to 1. Full audit trail to be pushed to immutable audit bucket.
jamie: +1. How do we stop someone from listing everything in the bucket?
elena: bucket ACLs deny list. presign lambda constructs object key, returns URL for that exact key. No list perms on escrow-role or requestor.
alex: on KMS side we need an EKM/alias that allows kms:Decrypt for the escrow-role but condition on kms:RequestTag/PrincipalTag or kms:EncryptionContext to limit usage to specific object and ticket id. Can add a kms:ViaService condition for extra safety.
maria: Sizing Q: will we be unwrapping logs older than our retention window (90 days)? Compliance might push back if we start exposing >365d. What's the expected retention profile for these escrow exports?
elena: We shouldn't change retention. Escrow only for logs that still exist in archive (within retention). For >365d we need legal/compliance signoff; default policy is no ad-hoc access beyond retention.
devops: Implementation idea: a small escrow service (lambda + SQS) that takes ticket id, object path, and approval token, performs KMS decrypt under escrow-role, generates a presigned URL with single-download lifecycle, and logs metadata to audit-bucket with immutable retention.
sec-bot: SEC-4523 created (https://rwd/SEC-4523) — initial ticket and checklist added.
noah: for incident response we need a breakglass path. suggest: emergency token generator that creates 1-hour access but must be logged and triggers immediate pager to sec channel and postmortem flag. Two-person approval can be waived only by CISO + oncall with recorded justification.
jamie: also require automated PII redaction step for exported blobs. we can run a lightweight scrubber before presign. If scrubber fails, escalate to sec for manual redaction.
elena: Agreed. Proposed minimal requirements in RFC: 1) Ticket + justification 2) Two approvers (sec + oncall) for normal requests 3) Breakglass with CISO+oncall and mandatory postmortem 4) presigned URL single-download, TTL 24h 5) escrow-role KMS:Decrypt conditioned on ticket/object 6) no list perms anywhere 7) PII scrub and audit dump to immutable bucket 8) retention guardrails enforced (no ad-hoc > retention window)
alex: IAM snippet (rough) — keep scope minimal:
```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/escrow-key",
  "Condition": {
    "StringEquals": {"kms:EncryptionContext:TicketID": "SEC-4523"}
  }
}
```
noah: solid. Who owns the RFC and next steps?
elena: I'll draft RFC in rwd-infra/rfcs and open a small PR for the lambda + IAM changes. tagging @noah for RBAC review and @devops for infra implementation.
maria: :thumbsup: please cc compliance once RFC is up.
devops: will estimate and attach to SEC-4523.
elena: ok — I'll push RFC by EOD tomorrow and include test plan (smoke decrypts, audit checks, download-count enforcement).
